title: Updates to Hobby and Pro Terms of Service
description: We are updating the Terms of Service for Hobby and Pro customers, effective October 19, 2026. The updates clarify some existing Vercel practices, expand terms on topics such as managed accounts and credits, and reflect applicable legal requirements, including certain cancellation and service-change rights for eligible consumers in the UK and EU. Credits and billing A new section sets out how credits work: plan-included credits expire at the end of the subscription term and purchased credits expire one year after purchase unless stated otherwise in the relevant credit purchase terms. Credits can only be used to pay Vercel fees, have no cash value, and are nontransferable. Credits are generally nonrefundable, but unused purchased credits are refunded if Vercel terminates your account without cause. The Terms also clarify that credit purchases are billed in advance, subscriptions auto-renew unless you turn off renewal, and third-party pass-through rates may change when provider rates change. ⁠⁠ Managed accounts The Terms now have a dedicated section for accounts that use a company email domain (e.g., work email), clarifying that the company can manage only the Projects you create inside its Team. We also clarified that if your company wishes to manage your account using your company work email, Vercel will now notify you first and give you a reasonable amount of time to move your personal content to an account with a different email address Renewal and cancellation You can turn off auto-renewal and cancel or downgrade through account settings or Support. Cancellation or downgrade generally takes effect at the start of the next renewal period. The Terms also explain statutory withdrawal and refund rights for eligible consumers. Service changes Eligible consumers in the UK and EU may cancel the affected subscription free of charge if a change has more than a minor negative impact on their access to or use of the Services. They have 30 days from notice or the change, whichever is later, and may receive a prorated refund of prepaid amounts for the remaining period. Other updates The service-specific provisions have been moved to a dedicated Service Terms page . The Terms also clarify sanctions-related obligations, including that use of the Services must not be in connection with or for the benefit of a sanctioned person under applicable laws. Read the full Terms of Service and Service Terms for details. Read more

title: Mercury 3 now available on AI Gateway
description: Mercury 3 from Inception is now available on AI Gateway with 50% off launch pricing. Inception reports strong results across a range of benchmarks, with generation speeds above 1,000 tokens per second. Mercury 3 uses diffusion to generate text through parallel refinement. It brings improved reasoning to latency-sensitive workloads such as browser agents, real-time search, interactive education, and customer support. A 1M-token context window gives those applications room for long documents and extended conversation histories. Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in your environment. Use inception/mercury-3 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select inception/mercury-3 in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Mercury 3 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash now available on AI Gateway for free
description: MiniMax M3.1 Flash from MiniMax is now available on AI Gateway for free until Oct 22. MiniMax M3.1 Flash is an open-weight multimodal model for coding and agentic work, with a 1M-token context window for long documents and multi-step agent sessions. Compared with earlier MiniMax models, M3.1 Flash improves on complex agentic tasks, coding, and cybersecurity. For coding, MiniMax reports its best results on application development, particularly frontend interactions, targeted bug fixes, and component tests. The free rate applies only when MiniMax serves the request. To make sure it does, sort the provider with order in the gateway provider options . After the offer ends, pinned requests bill at MiniMax's standard rate. Call it through the AI SDK , the Chat Completions , Responses , and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. See the coding agents guide for details. Try MiniMax M3.1 Flash in the model playground . title: Python on Vercel is now generally available
description: Python is now a first-class language and runtime on Vercel. Build APIs, full-stack applications, and AI agents with native Python SDKs and a shared development and deployment workflow for your Python backend and JavaScript frontend. Python framework and runtime support Vercel handles the infrastructure so you can focus on your application: Automatic framework support: FastAPI, Flask, and Django applications are automatically recognized and configured, with framework-specific support for serving static assets through the Vercel CDN. Native Python runtime and tooling: Vercel runs CPython on Linux and supports uv and pyproject.toml for dependency management. Compute for APIs and workers: Scale request-driven applications with Fluid compute and run long-running pull-based workloads with Vercel Daemons. Native Python SDKs Within your application, Python SDKs let you build agents, run untrusted code, and orchestrate durable workflows. Sandbox : Give your application or agent an isolated Linux VM on demand. AI SDK for Python (Beta): Generate or stream model responses and call tools. Get started with uv add ai . Workflow SDK for Python (Beta): Persist execution state and retry failed workflow steps. Queues (Beta): Send and receive messages for background work. Connect : Obtain credentials for calling external APIs. Blob : Upload and retrieve files in object storage. Use the SDKs individually or combine them in the same Python application. Your frontend and backend, together For full-stack applications, Vercel Services allows you to deploy your frontend and backends together in one project, with shared previews and atomic deployments and rollbacks. Within that project, you can view logs by service and connect backends privately through service bindings. For a frontend in frontend/ and a FastAPI app defined in backend/main.py , add this vercel.toml at the repository root. Requests under /api/ reach matching FastAPI routes with the path unchanged, while other requests reach the frontend. Run both services locally with vercel dev , then deploy them together from the same repository. Read the Python documentation to get started. Read more

title: TypeSafe AI's Jev 1.14 is now available on AI Gateway
description: Jev 1.14 from TypeSafe AI is now available on AI Gateway . Jev is a decision model for software. You pass it state and a set of questions, and it returns typed Choice, Score, and Boolean answers with probabilities instead of free-form text. It answers every question in one request, in parallel, for classification, routing, scoring, and automated verification. Jev 1.14 accepts images as part of the state, and has an experimental long-context mode for documents, logs, or conversation histories that are too long for a standard request. Use typesafe-ai/jev-1.14.0 as the model name. Image input Pass an image as a file part alongside text in state . This example reads a local PNG and asks a Boolean question about its color: Long context Enable long-context mode with providerOptions.typesafe.longContext: true . This example reads a support log and checks whether it reports a damaged delivery: Jev supports Zero Data Retention and No Training , which you can enable per request. Decision calls also appear in logs and custom reporting , count toward budgets , and accept other Gateway provider options in the same providerOptions.gateway object. Read the documentation on decision models on AI Gateway for more details, discover practical use cases for Jev , and browse resources in the knowledge base . Read more

title: MAI-Image-2.6 and MAI-Image-2.6-Flash now available on AI Gateway
description: MAI-Image-2.6 and MAI-Image-2.6-Flash from Microsoft are now available on AI Gateway . Generate images from text or edit existing images through the AI SDK or the AI CLI , with one API key and no provider account. Both models support photorealistic imagery, text rendering, and targeted edits to products, portraits, and layouts. You can provide up to five reference images to guide edits or combine subjects, with output sizes up to 1536 × 1536. MAI-Image-2.6 ( microsoft/mai-image-2.6 ) for final assets, when image quality matters more than speed. MAI-Image-2.6-Flash ( microsoft/mai-image-2.6-flash ) for faster generation at a lower cost, when you need many iterations, such as exploring prompts or generating variations. Use microsoft/mai-image-2.6 or microsoft/mai-image-2.6-flash as the model ID. To generate an image, call generateImage with a text prompt: Edit images by passing it as input with an instruction: Try MAI Image 2.6 and MAI Image 2.6 Flash in the model playground , or see the image generation guide . title: Repository checkout and Git LFS downloads are now faster
description: Repository checkout and Git LFS downloads are now faster on Vercel, reducing the time spent preparing your project's files before a build. During rollout on build machines with more than two vCPUs: The average time to get project files ready fell by 20%. For LFS-enabled projects, the average time to get project files ready fell by 54%, saving approximately 13 seconds per deployment on this step. The 90th-percentile time to get project files ready fell by 22%. This means 90% of deployments finish this step in that time or less. These improvements apply automatically, with no action required. Read the Git deployment documentation to learn more. Read more
